device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

The new-version card on Home is committed, and every button on it works in the real app. I found nothing to fix, so the commit is the same as before: `92e4b3dc69`, on branch `claude/home-update-card`. I haven't pushed it.

**How I tested it.** I ran a copy of the build with its own data folder. Instead of GitHub, I pointed its update check at a small local server that pretends version 2.0.2 is out. So no click reached GitHub and nothing changed in your own JusPrin data.

From 2026-11-08, JusPrin app work lands on `jusprin-dev`. Kenneth: "branch out a jusprin-dev from the upstream merge commit, and use this branch as the dev branch". It starts at `975c703f08` (the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 into ui-walkthrough) and contains `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those. AGENTS.md's "Branches" section records this. `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1. Server code in tsd-enterprise goes straight to `master` (2026-11-06 rule, unchanged).

History: 2026-11-06 `jusprin-newui-integration`; 2026-11-07 `ui-walkthrough`; 2026-11-08 `jusprin-dev`.

`main`, Kenneth 2026-11-08: "main will be the stable branch that doesn't allow force push ( except in some extreme circumstances when no other options are feasible). This is so that the users who clone our repo won't have to force pull." and "for now, it also double a release branch. But this rule is more flexible than the first one." GitHub branch protection on `main` blocks force pushes and deletion, admins included (enforce_admins). `main` moves forward from `jusprin-dev` only when a version is released; ask before fast-forwarding it. On 2026-11-08 Kenneth chose to leave `main` at 4da9d7beb4 until 2.0.0 ships, although that means the scheduled nightly keeps running `main`'s older file and doesn't build `jusprin-dev` until then. Start the nightly by hand on `jusprin-dev` with only `-f sign_macos=true`. GitHub runs scheduled workflows from `main`'s copy of the file, and validates dispatch inputs against it.

**Why:** the dev branch is the build Kenneth reviews; work on a side branch never reaches what he tests.

**How to apply:** Kenneth, 2026-11-08: "I want the main checkout to be always on jusprin-dev". Since then /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin holds `jusprin-dev`; byoai-newui was moved to its own branch `byoai-newui`. Git allows one checkout per branch, so never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. Commit from a worktree of your own on its own branch or detached at the tip. Then bring the main checkout along so its files match the branch; moving the ref from elsewhere (update-ref, or a push without a pull) leaves the main checkout's `git status` showing the new commits as reversed. When pushing is asked: push to origin jusprin-dev, then `git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin pull --ff-only` (Kenneth: "you just need to bring the local main checkout by pulling from the remote"). Push nothing unless asked. Supersedes the landing question in [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]].

The same day the main session missed that side-thread answer and landed it with `git merge --no-ff` (8838af0820) and pushed it. With Kenneth's yes it was replaced by the plain commit 12e1529cb6 (force-push with lease) minutes later.

**Why:** jusprin-dev's history is what Kenneth reads; merge commits for one-commit branches are noise.

**How to apply:** land a branch on jusprin-dev as plain commits (cherry-pick, or rebase then fast-forward). # Windows "install and restart" prototype: what happened on the VM

Measured 2026-11-19 on the GCP Windows test VM (jusprin-win-test, Windows Server 2022, no GPU).
It started from JusPrin 2.0.0 installed in C:\Program Files\JusPrin and the real %APPDATA%\JusPrin2 data folder,
which has 4 projects, an Anker M5 printer and an Anthropic API key. Nothing was committed or landed.
The test program is updater_proto.cpp in this folder. It compiles the app's own src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp
against the deps on the VM (build.cmd). The test scripts are common.ps1 and c1/c2/c3.ps1, and helper-log.txt is its log.

## Measured

- Download: `Slic3r::Http::get(<release url>)` fetched the 192 MB installer in 3.2 s. That is GCP bandwidth; a home connection will be slower.
  Checking it against SHA256SUMS.txt took 3.4 s and the sums matched.
- The downloaded file has no Zone.Identifier stream (no "downloaded from the internet" mark).
- From a normal-user process (medium integrity, started through Explorer):
  - `CreateProcessW("<installer> /S")` fails with error 740 (requires elevation). The installer's manifest says `requireAdministrator`.
  - `ShellExecuteExW(verb "open", "<installer>", "/S")` shows the UAC prompt (consent.exe). No SmartScreen step runs first.
    The prompt is on the secure desktop, so my screenshot tool could not capture it ("The handle is invalid").
- The same file with Edge's mark (ZoneId=3), opened from Explorer, shows SmartScreen's "Windows protected your PC"; "More info" shows
  "Publisher: Unknown publisher" plus "Run anyway". Downloading it in Edge first shows "isn't commonly downloaded. Make sure you trust …".
  For the double-click test I wrote Edge's mark onto a copy myself, because Edge's download panel ignored synthetic clicks.
- Defender reported no detections (Get-MpThreatDetection was empty).
- `/S` works. Fresh install: 33 s, exit 0. It installs per-machine to C:\Program Files\JusPrin, uninstall key HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\…\Uninstall\JusPrin.
  With the installer's own "Run JusPrin" step skipped in silent mode, nothing relaunches the app.
- **The app still open:** the installer exits 0 and the registry says 2.0.1, but orca-slicer.exe, OrcaSlicer.dll and ~50 other DLLs stay at 2.0.0
  while ~18,850 resource files become 2.0.1. The running app keeps going. A restart runs the mixed install. Running the installer again after quitting repairs it.
- **The app just quit:** 45 s, exit 0, every file 2.0.1.
- **Helper flow** (elevated helper waits for the app's PID, runs `installer /S`, then `explorer.exe "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe"`):
  the app took 11 s to close, the install 136 s, the new process appeared at 152 s and the window at 190 s. The new app is not elevated (parent is Explorer).
  Same 4 projects, same printer. JusPrin2.conf is unchanged except `last_backup_path` and its checksum line. 1,841 data files before and after.
- Install time varied from 45 to 136 s for the same upgrade on this VM.
- Disk full (600 MB free, caused by another session plus my files) made `/S` exit 2 halfway. That left a half-copied folder and no uninstall entry.

## Inferred, not measured

- Windows 11 Smart App Control checks every unsigned program however it is started, mark or no mark (secondary sources only).
  Server 2022 has no Smart App Control, so this VM cannot show it.
- Http keeps the whole body in memory before on_complete; a real version should stream to a file.

## In-app run, Kenneth pressing the button (2026-11-19, 19:26 VM time)

Build: JusPrin 2.0.0 plus throwaway commit cc69feae92 (branch proto/win-install-restart-from-2.0.0, not pushed).
Preferences › Updates › Download downloads the installer with Slic3r::Http, checks it against SHA256SUMS.txt,
starts a helper with a UAC request, and quits. The elevated helper waits for the app to exit, runs `installer /S`, then reopens the app through Explorer.
Timeline from in-app-kenneth-run-log.txt (app, helper and a window watcher write the same file):

| seconds after click | what happened |
|---|---|
| 0.0 | click; progress window "Downloading JusPrin 2.0.1…" |
| 9.2 | 192 MB downloaded |
| 10.6 | checksum matches; UAC prompt up |
| 16.8 | Kenneth clicks Yes; JusPrin's windows close at 17.1, process gone at 17.6 |
| 17.9 – 57.1 | installer runs 39 s, exit 0; nothing on screen |
| 57.1 | helper reads orca-slicer.exe version 2.0.1, reopens JusPrin |
| 69.4 | JusPrin 2.0.1 window up |

Measured after: registry 2.0.1, orca-slicer.exe 2.0.1, log says build 4f73c65c; the app is not elevated; same 4 projects,
Anker M5, Anthropic key and settings. Cancelling UAC (dry run) leaves 2.0.0 running with "The update was cancelled. JusPrin was not changed."
Not tested in this run: a signed-in JusPrin account (the app stayed on the Anthropic key) and an unsaved project (the title said "Saved").
On the VM only, the helper copies the Mesa software-OpenGL DLL back after the install.

## Showing progress during the install (2026-11-19)

Kenneth asked how hard it is to show progress during the minute or so when the
app has closed and nothing is on screen. Two ways were built and each run once
on jusprin-win-test, started by a script (not by Kenneth's click).

### A. The helper draws its own small window (screenshots 10, 11)
Measured: "Closing JusPrin…" with a moving bar, then "Installing JusPrin 2.0.1…"
with a filling bar, then "Opening JusPrin 2.0.1…" until the JusPrin window is
visible, then it closes. Install 41.0 s (silent, same as before). JusPrin window
14.1 s after the installer ended. The bar is bytes written by the installer
divided by the size of the current install (672 MB); the installer wrote 618 MB,
so the bar stopped at 92% and jumped to 100%. Installer unchanged. About 150
lines of plain Win32 in the helper (comctl32 progress bar, DPI aware, UTF-8).

### B. The installer shows only its own "Installing" page (screenshots 12-14)
Measured: the stock NSIS page "Installing / Please wait while JusPrin is being
installed" with "Extract: <file>" and a bar; no Welcome or Finish page. Before it,
about 8 s of empty desktop while the helper silently uninstalls the old version
(screenshot 13). Install 60.1 s, about 19 s slower than silent. Exit code 0 after
the SetErrorLevel fix; the splash was up within 10 s of the installer
closing (screenshot 14), main window 12.1 s after it closed. 18,860 files, Start-menu shortcut present.
Changes: installer.nsh (a /PASSIVE switch that posts a jump past five pages and
quits at the end of the install section), one CPACK_NSIS_EXTRA_INSTALL_COMMANDS
line, and the helper running the old Uninstall.exe /S first because CPack's
"uninstall the old version?" box only answers itself in silent mode.
Diff: installer-passive-page.diff.

### Comparison
- A covers the whole gap (closing, uninstall, install, reopening); B leaves the
  uninstall and the reopening blank.
- A keeps the faster silent install; B costs about 19 s.
- B depends on CPack's page order (a hard-coded count of 5) and on the old
  version being uninstalled by the helper; A changes no installer code.
- A's bar estimate needs a better target size (for example the new version's
  installed size published beside the installer); B's bar is exact.

### Decision (2026-11-19)
Kenneth: "Go with option one, don't clean up." Option one is A above: the update
helper draws its own progress window; the installer is not changed. The VM
(test build installed, Ipr* tasks, C:\guitest\ipr) and the unpushed branch
proto/win-install-restart-from-2.0.0 are kept as they are.

# Windows "install and restart" prototype: what happened on the VM

Measured 2026-11-19 on the GCP Windows test VM (jusprin-win-test, Windows Server 2022, no GPU).
It started from JusPrin 2.0.0 installed in C:\Program Files\JusPrin and the real %APPDATA%\JusPrin2 data folder,
which has 4 projects, an Anker M5 printer and an Anthropic API key. Nothing was committed or landed.
The test program is updater_proto.cpp in this folder. It compiles the app's own src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp
against the deps on the VM (build.cmd). The test scripts are common.ps1 and c1/c2/c3.ps1, and helper-log.txt is its log.

## Measured

- Download: `Slic3r::Http::get(<release url>)` fetched the 192 MB installer in 3.2 s. That is GCP bandwidth; a home connection will be slower.
  Checking it against SHA256SUMS.txt took 3.4 s and the sums matched.
- The downloaded file has no Zone.Identifier stream (no "downloaded from the internet" mark).
- From a normal-user process (medium integrity, started through Explorer):
  - `CreateProcessW("<installer> /S")` fails with error 740 (requires elevation). The installer's manifest says `requireAdministrator`.
  - `ShellExecuteExW(verb "open", "<installer>", "/S")` shows the UAC prompt (consent.exe). No SmartScreen step runs first.
    The prompt is on the secure desktop, so my screenshot tool could not capture it ("The handle is invalid").
- The same file with Edge's mark (ZoneId=3), opened from Explorer, shows SmartScreen's "Windows protected your PC"; "More info" shows
  "Publisher: Unknown publisher" plus "Run anyway". Downloading it in Edge first shows "isn't commonly downloaded. Make sure you trust …".
  For the double-click test I wrote Edge's mark onto a copy myself, because Edge's download panel ignored synthetic clicks.
- Defender reported no detections (Get-MpThreatDetection was empty).
- `/S` works. Fresh install: 33 s, exit 0. It installs per-machine to C:\Program Files\JusPrin, uninstall key HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\…\Uninstall\JusPrin.
  With the installer's own "Run JusPrin" step skipped in silent mode, nothing relaunches the app.
- **The app still open:** the installer exits 0 and the registry says 2.0.1, but orca-slicer.exe, OrcaSlicer.dll and ~50 other DLLs stay at 2.0.0
  while ~18,850 resource files become 2.0.1. The running app keeps going. A restart runs the mixed install. Running the installer again after quitting repairs it.
- **The app just quit:** 45 s, exit 0, every file 2.0.1.
- **Helper flow** (elevated helper waits for the app's PID, runs `installer /S`, then `explorer.exe "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe"`):
  the app took 11 s to close, the install 136 s, the new process appeared at 152 s and the window at 190 s. The new app is not elevated (parent is Explorer).
  Same 4 projects, same printer. JusPrin2.conf is unchanged except `last_backup_path` and its checksum line. 1,841 data files before and after.
- Install time varied from 45 to 136 s for the same upgrade on this VM.
- Disk full (600 MB free, caused by another session plus my files) made `/S` exit 2 halfway. That left a half-copied folder and no uninstall entry.

## Inferred, not measured

- Windows 11 Smart App Control checks every unsigned program however it is started, mark or no mark (secondary sources only).
  Server 2022 has no Smart App Control, so this VM cannot show it.
- Http keeps the whole body in memory before on_complete; a real version should stream to a file.

## In-app run, Kenneth pressing the button (2026-11-19, 19:26 VM time)

Build: JusPrin 2.0.0 plus throwaway commit cc69feae92 (branch proto/win-install-restart-from-2.0.0, not pushed).
Preferences › Updates › Download downloads the installer with Slic3r::Http, checks it against SHA256SUMS.txt,
starts a helper with a UAC request, and quits. The elevated helper waits for the app to exit, runs `installer /S`, then reopens the app through Explorer.
Timeline from in-app-kenneth-run-log.txt (app, helper and a window watcher write the same file):

| seconds after click | what happened |
|---|---|
| 0.0 | click; progress window "Downloading JusPrin 2.0.1…" |
| 9.2 | 192 MB downloaded |
| 10.6 | checksum matches; UAC prompt up |
| 16.8 | Kenneth clicks Yes; JusPrin's windows close at 17.1, process gone at 17.6 |
| 17.9 – 57.1 | installer runs 39 s, exit 0; nothing on screen |
| 57.1 | helper reads orca-slicer.exe version 2.0.1, reopens JusPrin |
| 69.4 | JusPrin 2.0.1 window up |

Measured after: registry 2.0.1, orca-slicer.exe 2.0.1, log says build 4f73c65c; the app is not elevated; same 4 projects,
Anker M5, Anthropic key and settings. Cancelling UAC (dry run) leaves 2.0.0 running with "The update was cancelled. JusPrin was not changed."
Not tested in this run: a signed-in JusPrin account (the app stayed on the Anthropic key) and an unsaved project (the title said "Saved").
On the VM only, the helper copies the Mesa software-OpenGL DLL back after the install.

## Showing progress during the install (2026-11-19)

Kenneth asked how hard it is to show progress during the minute or so when the
app has closed and nothing is on screen. Two ways were built and each run once
on jusprin-win-test, started by a script (not by Kenneth's click).

### A. The helper draws its own small window (screenshots 10, 11)
Measured: "Closing JusPrin…" with a moving bar, then "Installing JusPrin 2.0.1…"
with a filling bar, then "Opening JusPrin 2.0.1…" until the JusPrin window is
visible, then it closes. Install 41.0 s (silent, same as before). JusPrin window
14.1 s after the installer ended. The bar is bytes written by the installer
divided by the size of the current install (672 MB); the installer wrote 618 MB,
so the bar stopped at 92% and jumped to 100%. Installer unchanged. About 150
lines of plain Win32 in the helper (comctl32 progress bar, DPI aware, UTF-8).

### B. The installer shows only its own "Installing" page (screenshots 12-14)
Measured: the stock NSIS page "Installing / Please wait while JusPrin is being
installed" with "Extract: <file>" and a bar; no Welcome or Finish page. Before it,
about 8 s of empty desktop while the helper silently uninstalls the old version
(screenshot 13). Install 60.1 s, about 19 s slower than silent. Exit code 0 after
the SetErrorLevel fix; the splash was up within 10 s of the installer
closing (screenshot 14), main window 12.1 s after it closed. 18,860 files, Start-menu shortcut present.
Changes: installer.nsh (a /PASSIVE switch that posts a jump past five pages and
quits at the end of the install section), one CPACK_NSIS_EXTRA_INSTALL_COMMANDS
line, and the helper running the old Uninstall.exe /S first because CPack's
"uninstall the old version?" box only answers itself in silent mode.
Diff: installer-passive-page.diff.

### Comparison
- A covers the whole gap (closing, uninstall, install, reopening); B leaves the
  uninstall and the reopening blank.
- A keeps the faster silent install; B costs about 19 s.
- B depends on CPack's page order (a hard-coded count of 5) and on the old
  version being uninstalled by the helper; A changes no installer code.
- A's bar estimate needs a better target size (for example the new version's
  installed size published beside the installer); B's bar is exact.

### Decision (2026-11-19)
Kenneth: "Go with option one, don't clean up." Option one is A above: the update
helper draws its own progress window; the installer is not changed. The VM
(test build installed, Ipr* tasks, C:\guitest\ipr) and the unpushed branch
proto/win-install-restart-from-2.0.0 are kept as they are.

content.content:
It's moderately hard. With a full "Install and restart" button, I estimate two to three weeks of work, and most of the risk is on Windows. A smaller version, where the app downloads the installer and opens it for the person, would take a few days. Both figures are my estimates, not measurements.

**What JusPrin ships today**

- **Mac:** a signed and notarised disk image, so Apple accepts it as coming from us.
- **Windows:** an unsigned installer, plus a zip that runs without installing.
- **Linux:** an AppImage, a single file that runs as is.

OrcaSlicer has no in-app installer either, so there's nothing upstream to reuse.

**What "install and restart" takes on each platform**

- **Mac, about 3–5 days.** Sparkle is the standard tool for this. It downloads the update, checks it, swaps the app in place and relaunches. We would add Sparkle to the app bundle and keep a private signing key in the release workflow. Each release then signs its disk image and publishes a small list of versions for the app to read. The signing step needs care: Sparkle's helper programs must be signed one by one before the app itself ([Sparkle's publishing docs](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/publishing/), [one developer's write-up of the pitfalls](https://steipete.me/posts/2025/code-signing-and-notarization-sparkle-and-tears)).
- **Windows, about 3–5 days, plus a decision for you.** WinSparkle, or our own code, would download the installer, check its signature, close JusPrin and run the installer silently. Our installer accepts the standard silent switch, `/S`. The catch is that our installer is unsigned. Having the app download and run an unsigned program on its own is the riskiest part of the whole plan, so the app must at least check a signature of our own on every download. Antivirus programs may also flag it. I haven't confirmed whether Windows' download warning (SmartScreen) fires for an installer the app downloads itself, so that has to be tested. Buying a Windows code-signing certificate removes most of this risk.
- **Linux, about 2–3 days.** AppImage has its own update mechanism, AppImageUpdate, which downloads only the parts of the file that changed ([AppImage docs](https://docs.appimage.org/packaging-guide/optional/updates.html)).

**What auto-update can't reach**

- People already on 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 must install the next version by hand once.
- The Windows zip and Microsoft Store installs can't update themselves. Store installs get updates from the Store anyway.
- A bug in the updater can strand people on that version, so each release needs a test of updating from the previous one.

**The smaller version.** PrusaSlicer does this in [its updater](https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer/blob/master/src/slic3r/Utils/AppUpdater.cpp). It downloads the file inside the app. On Windows it runs the installer, and on Mac it opens the disk image in Finder for the person to drag across. On Linux it only downloads the file. That saves the trip to GitHub, but on Mac people still drag the app themselves. One person on Prusa's forum reported that the Mac update didn't replace the old app ([forum thread](https://forum.prusa3d.com/forum/prusaslicer/problems-with-automatic-update)).

**Decision needed: should JusPrin install updates itself, or only download them?**
- **Install and restart.** About two to three weeks, plus a Windows code-signing certificate if you want the Windows side safe and free of warnings. The card on Home would then offer "Install and restart" instead of "Open download page".
- **Download in the app only.** A few days. The person still runs the installer or drags the app, as today, just without visiting GitHub.
- **Keep the current card.** No extra work. People keep downloading from GitHub themselves.

My pick is Install and restart, built Mac first with Sparkle because that path is the most proven, and Windows only once the signing question is settled. Either way the card on Home is still needed, and only its buttons change.
=====
The new-version card for Home is now on the canvas, redrawn so that JusPrin downloads the update itself. It's on the "Updating JusPrin" page at https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ#page-updating, boards 07 to 15. Nothing is built yet. These are proposals for you to approve.

**What the person sees, step by step**
- **Card appears:** when the update check finds 2.0.1, a card shows at the top of Home's right column. It offers Download, Remind me tomorrow and Skip this version.
- **Downloading:** pressing Download saves the file to the Downloads folder while they keep working. The card shows "212 MB of 475 MB" with a Cancel button. If JusPrin quits mid-download, the download starts over next time.
- **Download finished:** the card's button saves unsaved changes and quits JusPrin. Then:
  - **Mac:** it opens the disk image. The disk image window itself says what to do: drag JusPrin onto Applications, choose Replace, then open JusPrin from the Dock. It has to work this way because I checked on this Mac that Finder refuses to replace an app that's running.
  - **Windows:** it runs the installer, and the person opens JusPrin from the Start menu afterwards.
  - **Linux:** it puts 2.0.1 in place of the running AppImage and starts it.
- **After updating:** the first time 2.0.1 opens, the card says "You're now on JusPrin 2.0.1" and offers to move the installer to the Trash.
- **Connection lost:** if the download stops because the connection dropped, the card says so and offers Try again.

**Cold-reader checks.** Fresh agents read only the screenshots, three times. I fixed what they misread. For example, "your current JusPrin file" on Linux sounded like it would overwrite a project, and "Replace" on the Mac sounded like it would delete projects.

**Decision needed: the offline message.** Board 13 tells the person "Your computer lost its internet connection. Check it, then try again." Under the error-handling rules, a message of its own counts as an expected error, and each one needs your yes. Every other download failure would get the usual "Something went wrong on our side" message and a report. My pick is to approve it, because checking the connection is something the person can actually do. The box below asks it.

**Decision needed: Linux goes one step past "download only".** If JusPrin only downloaded the new AppImage, the person's menu and desktop shortcuts would keep opening 2.0.0. The options:
- **Do nothing more:** the person has to replace the file by hand, and most won't know they need to.
- **Rename the new file over the running one, then start it:** a few lines of code, and safe on Linux because the running copy keeps its file open.

My pick is the rename. Do you agree that JusPrin should replace the AppImage on Linux?

**Decision needed: save before quitting.** The cards promise that unsaved changes are kept when JusPrin quits to install. I haven't checked that quitting saves the open project today. The proposal is that the button calls autosave's save-now first. The alternative is to drop the promise from the card. A worried reader asked about exactly this, so my pick is to save first. Should the install button save the open project before quitting?

**Not verified yet**
- A running print keeps going while JusPrin is quit and reinstalled, for every connection type.
- Whether a file JusPrin downloads itself triggers a Gatekeeper or SmartScreen warning. [Prototype Windows install-and-restart on the VM](#local_dd7ca455-eee4-4e50-8ebf-f8bf1b869b32) is measuring this on Windows and is still running. Its branch starts from `main`, so I'll check what it reports before passing it on.

The card reaches people only from the first release that includes it. 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 will never show it.
=====

**Decision needed: should JusPrin install updates itself, or only download them?**
- **Install and restart.** About two to three weeks, plus a Windows code-signing certificate if you want the Windows side safe and free of warnings. The card on Home would then offer "Install and restart" instead of "Open download page".
- **Download in the app only.** A few days. The person still runs the installer or drags the app, as today, just without visiting GitHub.
- **Keep the current card.** No extra work. People keep downloading from GitHub themselves.

My pick is Install and restart, built Mac first with Sparkle because that path is the most proven, and Windows only once the signing question is settled. Either way the card on Home is still needed, and only its buttons change.
=====
The new-version card for Home is now on the canvas, redrawn so that JusPrin downloads the update itself. It's on the "Updating JusPrin" page at https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ#page-updating, boards 07 to 15. Nothing is built yet. These are proposals for you to approve.

**What the person sees, step by step**
- **Card appears:** when the update check finds 2.0.1, a card shows at the top of Home's right column. It offers Download, Remind me tomorrow and Skip this version.
- **Downloading:** pressing Download saves the file to the Downloads folder while they keep working. The card shows "212 MB of 475 MB" with a Cancel button. If JusPrin quits mid-download, the download starts over next time.
- **Download finished:** the card's button saves unsaved changes and quits JusPrin. Then:
  - **Mac:** it opens the disk image. The disk image window itself says what to do: drag JusPrin onto Applications, choose Replace, then open JusPrin from the Dock. It has to work this way because I checked on this Mac that Finder refuses to replace an app that's running.
  - **Windows:** it runs the installer, and the person opens JusPrin from the Start menu afterwards.
  - **Linux:** it puts 2.0.1 in place of the running AppImage and starts it.
- **After updating:** the first time 2.0.1 opens, the card says "You're now on JusPrin 2.0.1" and offers to move the installer to the Trash.
- **Connection lost:** if the download stops because the connection dropped, the card says so and offers Try again.

**Cold-reader checks.** Fresh agents read only the screenshots, three times. I fixed what they misread. For example, "your current JusPrin file" on Linux sounded like it would overwrite a project, and "Replace" on the Mac sounded like it would delete projects.

**Decision needed: the offline message.** Board 13 tells the person "Your computer lost its internet connection. Check it, then try again." Under the error-handling rules, a message of its own counts as an expected error, and each one needs your yes. Every other download failure would get the usual "Something went wrong on our side" message and a report. My pick is to approve it, because checking the connection is something the person can actually do. The box below asks it.

**Decision needed: Linux goes one step past "download only".** If JusPrin only downloaded the new AppImage, the person's menu and desktop shortcuts would keep opening 2.0.0. The options:
- **Do nothing more:** the person has to replace the file by hand, and most won't know they need to.
- **Rename the new file over the running one, then start it:** a few lines of code, and safe on Linux because the running copy keeps its file open.

My pick is the rename. Do you agree that JusPrin should replace the AppImage on Linux?

**Decision needed: save before quitting.** The cards promise that unsaved changes are kept when JusPrin quits to install. I haven't checked that quitting saves the open project today. The proposal is that the button calls autosave's save-now first. The alternative is to drop the promise from the card. A worried reader asked about exactly this, so my pick is to save first. Should the install button save the open project before quitting?

**Not verified yet**
- A running print keeps going while JusPrin is quit and reinstalled, for every connection type.
- Whether a file JusPrin downloads itself triggers a Gatekeeper or SmartScreen warning. [Prototype Windows install-and-restart on the VM](#local_dd7ca455-eee4-4e50-8ebf-f8bf1b869b32) is measuring this on Windows and is still running. Its branch starts from `main`, so I'll check what it reports before passing it on.

The card reaches people only from the first release that includes it. 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 will never show it.

- **Architecture:** The SPUUserDriver protocol is used for implementing a user interface for the Sparkle updater. To build one, you write a class that conforms to the protocol and then create a SPUUpdater with your user driver instead of creating the typical SPUStandardUpdaterController. SPUUpdater and its delegate SPUUpdaterDelegate do not contain any user-interface or AppKit logic.
- **Install behavior:** The docs say the protocol is not used in a way that eliminates UI or installs updates silently. Your UI also needs to let the user be in control of installing an update once an update is found, since installs can trigger an authorization prompt.
- **Authorization:** If the state.stage is SPUUpdateStateNotDownloaded or SPUUpdateStateDownloaded the user may be presented an authorization prompt to install the update when authorization is required, for example if the update is a package install.
- **Focus method:** To support bringing an update back into focus, implement -[SPUUserDriver showUpdateInFocus]. This method used to be required but is now optional since Sparkle 2.8.
- **Build option:** A developer writing their own updater user interface may choose to build Sparkle with SPARKLE_BUILD_UI_BITS=0 which strips out the standard UI bits.
- **Reference implementations:** The repo includes SUPopUpTitlebarUserDriver: Alternative user interface to the Sparkle Test App and SUCommandLineUserDriver: User interface to the sparkle-cli tool, which are useful examples.

**Gap:** None of the results gave the specific method names for triggering an install from code, such as the calls for checking for updates or confirming an install. For those, check the SPUUpdater and SPUUserDriver API reference pages and the Sparkle 2 repo's Test App source.

content.text:
"Install and restart" is feasible. On Windows the prototype has now done the whole flow with your click, and nothing in it blocks a real build. I estimate three to four weeks for all three platforms, up from my earlier two to three. The Windows run turned up work I hadn't counted, and the Mac side hasn't been prototyped yet, so it carries the most uncertainty. These are my estimates, not measurements.

**What the Windows prototype showed on the test VM**
- **The full run.** You clicked Download in Preferences. JusPrin downloaded the 192 MB installer in 9 s and checked it against the release's checksum file. It then asked for administrator rights once and closed. A small helper program ran the installer silently and reopened JusPrin 2.0.1. The new window appeared 69 s after your click. Projects, the printer, the API key and settings were all unchanged, and the reopened app was not running as administrator.
- **SmartScreen.** No "Windows protected your PC" warning appeared. Windows only shows it for files a browser marks as downloaded, and the app's own download carries no mark. The admin prompt still says "Unknown publisher" on every update, because our installer is unsigned.
- **Hazards that real code must handle:**
  - If the installer runs while JusPrin is still open, it reports success but leaves old program files beside new ones. The helper avoids this by waiting until JusPrin has exited.
  - When the disk filled up, the installer stopped halfway. It left a broken folder and no uninstall entry.
  - Install time on the VM varied from 41 s to 136 s.
- **Progress window.** You chose for the helper to draw its own progress window while the app is closed. The bar currently stops at 92% because it compares against the old version's size.

**What the real version needs, per platform**
- **Windows, about 6–8 days.**
  - Build the helper and ship it inside the installer.
  - Save the download to a file instead of memory.
  - Before quitting, check free disk space, check for a second JusPrin window or an upload still being sent to a printer, and save the open project. JusPrin already has project autosave to reuse.
  - Have the release publish the installed size, so the bar fills correctly.
  - Report a helper failure on the next start. The helper runs while JusPrin is closed, so it can't use the app's own error report.
  - Run an end-to-end test on the VM.
- **Mac, about 5–8 days, untested.** Sparkle, the standard Mac updater, swaps the app and relaunches it. To keep the Home card as the only update screen, we'd give Sparkle our own interface, which Sparkle supports ([custom interfaces](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/custom-user-interfaces/), [SPUUserDriver](https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/api-reference/Protocols/SPUUserDriver.html)). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Turns OrcaSlicer's universal app into JusPrin.app and puts it in a disk image.
#
#   macos_package.sh <OrcaSlicer.app> <version> <output dir>
#
# OrcaSlicer's build names the bundle OrcaSlicer.app with OrcaSlicer's bundle
# identifier, icon and a "JusPrin <build id>" version string. This copies it to
# JusPrin.app and sets JusPrin's identity before anything is signed, because
# editing Info.plist afterwards would break the signature.
#
# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed by
# rcodesign (RCODESIGN) with the Developer ID certificate and key in the .p12
# file MACOS_P12_FILE, whose password is in the file MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE,
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. rcodesign reads
# the certificate itself, so no keychain is involved: Apple's codesign cannot
# use a keychain from a launchd daemon, such as the self-hosted Mac's runner,
# and fails there with errSecInternalComponent. Otherwise the app gets an
# ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only.
set -euo pipefail

source_app="$1"
version="$2"
out_dir="$3"

script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd -- "${script_dir}/../../../../.." && pwd)"
entitlements="${repo_root}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${repo_root}/scripts/retry.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
stage="${work}/dmg"
app="${stage}/JusPrin.app"
dmg="${out_dir}/JusPrin_Mac_universal_V${version}.dmg"
mkdir -p "${stage}" "${out_dir}"
cp -R "${source_app}" "${app}"

plist="${app}/Contents/Info.plist"
buddy=/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy
set_key() {
    "${buddy}" -c "Set :$1 $2" "${plist}" 2>/dev/null || "${buddy}" -c "Add :$1 string $2" "${plist}"
}
set_key CFBundleIdentifier io.obico.jusprin
set_key CFBundleName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleDisplayName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleShortVersionString "${version}"
set_key CFBundleVersion "${version}"
set_key CFBundleGetInfoString "JusPrin ${version}"
cp "${repo_root}/resources/jusprin/images/JusPrin.icns" "${app}/Contents/Resources/images/JusPrin.icns"
set_key CFBundleIconFile images/JusPrin.icns
plutil -lint "${plist}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml signs: --deep misses the bundled Python
    # runtime, and notarisation rejects any Mach-O file without the hardened
    # runtime signature, so each one is signed, then the bundle last.
    # The main executable is left to the bundle's signature: signed on its
    # own, codesign checks the jusprin-mcp beside it, which the universal
    # join left unsigned, and fails with "code object is not signed at all".
    # --for-notarization turns on the hardened runtime and Apple's time stamp.
    # Signing the bundle signs each file in it again, keeping the entitlements
    # each one was signed with.
    sign() {
        "${RCODESIGN}" sign --for-notarization --entitlements-xml-file "${entitlements}" \
            --p12-file "${MACOS_P12_FILE}" --p12-password-file "${MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE}" "$1"
    }
    main_executable="${app}/Contents/MacOS/$("${buddy}" -c "Print :CFBundleExecutable" "${plist}")"
    machos=()
    while IFS= read -r f; do machos+=("$f"); done < <(
        find "${app}" -type f -print0 |
            xargs -0 file --no-pad --mime-type -- |
            grep -v ' (for architecture ' |
            grep ': application/x-mach-binary$' |
            sed 's|: application/x-mach-binary$||' |
            grep -vxF "${main_executable}"
    )
    echo "signing ${#machos[@]} Mach-O files in ${app}"
    for f in "${machos[@]}"; do sign "$f"; done
    sign "${app}"
else
    codesign --deep --force --sign - "${app}"
fi
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "${app}"

ln -sfn /Applications "${stage}/Applications"
retry hdiutil create -volname "JusPrin" -srcfolder "${stage}" -ov -format UDZO "${dmg}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    "${RCODESIGN}" sign --p12-file "${MACOS_P12_FILE}" --p12-password-file "${MACOS_P12_PASSWORD_FILE}" "${dmg}"
    codesign --verify --verbose=2 "${dmg}"
    notary=(--apple-id "${APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT}" --team-id "${TEAM_ID}" --password "${APP_PWD}")
    # notarytool exits 0 when Apple rejects the image, so read the status and
    # print Apple's report, which names each file it rejected.
    result="$(xcrun notarytool submit "${dmg}" "${notary[@]}" --wait --output-format json)"
    echo "${result}"
    if [ "$(plutil -extract status raw - <<<"${result}")" != "Accepted" ]; then
        xcrun notarytool log "$(plutil -extract id raw - <<<"${result}")" "${notary[@]}"
        exit 1
    fi
    retry xcrun stapler staple "${dmg}"
fi

rm -rf "${work}"
echo "${dmg}"

The search didn't turn up anything specific to Sparkle 2. The results are general Sparkle and macOS translocation material, and most are older posts.

**What's going on:** Translocation is a macOS security behavior. Apps that carry a quarantine flag and are launched through Finder get run from a temporary, read-only location instead of where they sit. A Sparkle-based updater can't replace an app from there. One Sparkle community thread describes the same failure you're seeing ("Sparkle can't be updated, because it was opened from a read-only or a temporary location") and says the fix is to copy the app into Applications and relaunch it ([Sitely community](https://community.sitely.app/t/sparkle-cant-be-updated-error/450)). An Eclectic Light article notes that translocated apps that use self-updating mechanisms like Sparkle may not be able to work ([Eclectic Light](https://eclecticlight.co/2024/05/14/lost-in-translocation/?like_comment=95444)).

**Why moving it doesn't always fix it:** Moving the app out of Downloads usually removes the quarantine flag, but not reliably. Per the same Sitely post, Finder sometimes leaves the flag in place, and the suggested recovery is to move the app out of Downloads, move it back in, and move it out again. If that still fails, download a fresh copy. Another Eclectic Light piece reports that an app that has already been translocated keeps its quarantine flag until it's moved with Finder, and that moving it into a folder that is itself inside Applications doesn't help ([Eclectic Light](https://eclecticlight.co/2022/09/06/dont-run-that-app-where-it-landed-how-translocation-can-cause-crashes/?like_comment=77967)).

**Practical checks:** Confirm the app's real path in Activity Monitor (Executable Path in the process inspector). If it points into a temporary or randomized location, it's translocated. Move it to /Applications with Finder, relaunch it from there, and check the path again ([Eclectic Light](https://eclecticlight.co/2025/10/16/check-if-an-app-is-stuck-in-translocation/?like_comment=109110)).

I didn't find Sparkle 2 release notes or a known-issue report for this bug, so if you need that, check the Sparkle GitHub issues or the Sparkle community forum for the specific version.
